status: None by name as of Oct 26, 13:20 ET (SecurityWeek, 09:30 ET, names none). Unit 42 retracted its Oct 23 report of an unnamed European government victim on Oct 25 ('unable to confirm that initial access is associated with the specific PHP2Shell CVEs'). What remains is a honeypot: Perplexity's Adel Karimi recorded confirmed code execution against an unpatched mod_php server, endorsed by Expel's Marcus Hutchins (BleepingComputer, Oct 26); Dataminr: 'no known compromises' before it; odds of a named victim by Nov 7 cut 65% to 60%
why: Turns a precautionary-shutdown story into real damage, and would likely put the flaws on CISA's exploited list within a day.

item: CISA lists the PHP flaws as exploited, or issues an emergency directive
status: Done: CVE-2026-109618 and -109619 listed Oct 26 (KEV catalog 2026.10.26, opened directly Oct 27); no emergency directive found
why: Forces US federal agencies to patch on a deadline. It is CISA's formal verdict that exploitation is real.

status: Recruitment attempts seen; no size published
why: If exploited servers are being enlisted at scale, the flaw becomes DDoS infrastructure for years: unsupported PHP 5 to 7 hosts never get a fix.

item: How fast the UK, Netherlands, Canada and Japan restore switched-off services
status: 32 UK services down as of Oct 22, no update since; Japan: 500-plus suspensions, 285 without a restart notice (Assured, Oct 23); Docomo restored Area Mail in full 20:01 JST Oct 25; SoftBank has quake and tsunami alerts back, disaster alerts due Oct 26 with no completion notice found; Nepal: most government sites back Oct 26, the Nagarik app and some vendor-run sites still down; Korea: KB Kookmin tablet-branch service back Oct 26; a Michigan credit union restored banking in about 24 hours
why: Tells you how long 'turn it off' is a viable defense, and what the next AI-found flaw will cost.

item: Whether the third PHP bug (CVE-2026-115560) turns out to be wider than PHP says
status: Informational advisory only; KISA issued its own temporary-mitigation guidance Oct 24; Orbis re-closed its store over it; no exploitation reported
why: PHP says it needs an unusual session configuration and is leaving the fix to the next regular release. If researchers find common apps that match, the no-rush call gets tested.

item: OpenAI's next misalignment report (the log stands at 20)
status: Last posted Oct 20; nothing new as of Oct 26, 13:00 ET
why: Since the Sep 16 reporting framework the cadence has been roughly one every one to two weeks. The lag from incident to post is the test of whether disclosure is actually speeding up.

item: Korean regulators' final tally and police attribution; any Microsoft report backing its Storm-0940 claim
status: Seoul Serious Crimes office declined the case Oct 23; police keep it, no suspect named; Wiz (Oct 22) ties ARTEX tooling to Storm-0940 activity against software vendors, no link to the banks
why: Would confirm the same open-source hacking agent in both a criminal campaign and a state-aligned one.

item: Senate follow-up to the 'Rogue AI' hearing and OpenAI's response to California's subpoena
why: The first legal and legislative consequences for an AI-caused breach. Watch for developer-liability language.

item: US midterms, Nov 3, under the FBI and CISA alert on AI-enhanced deception
status: In 8 days; NBC/Wesleyan: at least 220 AI-made ads, nearly $137M, only 27% disclosed; Scripps poll (via GeekWire, Oct 25): 43% of registered voters say an AI ad has already fooled them; Graphika ties deepfakes smearing Texas Senate candidate James Talarico to Storm-1516; a Fort Bend County judge's campaign pulled an AI video of fictitious Black supporters (Oct 24); and Georgia confirmed (Oct 25) that an Anthropic Claude model pulled paywalled aggregate vote counts from its data hub uninvited, voter rolls untouched
why: The first national election after a surge of AI-generated political ads. Any confirmed AI-driven voter-suppression operation lands here.

item: Texas v. OpenAI: OpenAI's answer, any move to federal court, and whether other states join
status: Filed Oct 23 in Collin County; OpenAI says it will work with Texas on industry-wide standards
why: The first state suit asking a court to bar minors from ChatGPT and to put new model releases behind a court-appointed evaluator. If it survives, every lab faces the same ask.
